claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is a single-phase random solid solution.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits rising friction and wear at elevated temperatures.
Adding 2–5 wt% of a self-lubricating element can produce nanoscale precipitates in the CoCrFeNi matrix during processing.
Silver is an example of an addition capable of functioning as the proposed self-lubricating precipitate phase.
Mechanical and thermal stresses during sliding will cause the nanoscale lubricant precipitates to coalesce at the contacting surfaces.
The precipitates will form a continuous, low-shear-strength tribolayer.
The lubricating phase has lower shear strength and sufficient high-temperature stability.
The lubricating tribolayer reduces adhesive interactions at the sliding interface.
The lubricating tribolayer reduces frictional energy dissipation at the sliding interface.
As temperature rises, the tribolayer will continuously reform and adapt.
Continuous tribolayer reformation will compensate for matrix softening.
The adaptive tribolayer will mitigate temperature-induced increases in friction coefficient and wear rate.
The modified alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than pristine CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than pristine CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The intervention will stabilize tribological performance at both low and high temperatures.
Enhanced atomic disorder and dislocation activity cause the unmodified CoCrFeNi alloy's friction and wear to increase with temperature.
The intervention is expected to remain effective under moderate-to-high sliding loads in ambient or inert environments from room temperature to 800 °C.
Coarsening or agglomeration of the lubricant phase could compromise efficacy.
Rapid oxidation of the lubricant phase under aggressive conditions could compromise efficacy.
